source_text: Διὰ τοῦτο καὶ τὸ χρυσοφορεῖν καὶ τὸ ἐσθῆτι μαλακωτέρᾳ χρῆσθαι οὐ τέλεον περικοπτέον, χαλινωτέον δὲ τὰς ἀλόγους τῶν ὁρμῶν, μὴ εἰς τὸ ἁβροδίαιτον ἡμᾶς ἐνσείσωσιν φέρουσαι ὑπὸ πολλῆς τῆς ἀνέσεως ἐξαρπάσασαι· δεινὴ γὰρ ἡ τρυφὴ εἰς κόρον ἐξοκείλασα σκιρτῆσαι καὶ ἀναχαιτίσαι καὶ τὸν ἡνίοχον, [καὶ] τὸν παιδαγωγόν, ἀποσείσασθαι, ὃς πόρρωθεν ἀνακόπτων τὰς ἡνίας ἄγει καὶ φέρει πρὸς σωτηρίαν τὸν ἵππον τὸν ἀνθρώπειον, τὸ ἄλογον μέρος τῆς ψυχῆς τὸ περὶ ἡδονὰς καὶ ὀρέξεις ἐπιψόγους καὶ λίθους καὶ χρυσίον καὶ ἐσθῆτα ποικίλην καὶ τὴν ἄλλην χλιδὴν ἐκθηριούμενον· ἐκεῖνο μάλιστα ἐν νῷ ἔχοντες τὸ εἰρημένον ἁγίως »τὴν ἀναστροφὴν ὑμῶν ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἔχοντες καλήν, ἵνα ἐν ᾧ καταλαλοῦσιν ὑμῶν ὡς κακοποιῶν, ἐκ τῶν καλῶν ἔργων ἐποπτεύσαντες δοξάσωσι τὸν θεόν.« δίδωσιν οὖν ἡμῖν ὁ παιδαγωγὸς ἐσθῆτι χρῆσθαι τῇ λιτῇ, χρόᾳ δὲ τῇ λευκῇ, ὡς προειρήκαμεν, ἵνα μὴ τέχνῃ ποικιλλομένῃ, φύσει δὲ γεννωμένῃ οἰκειούμενοι, πᾶν ὅσον ἀπατηλὸν καὶ τῆς ἀληθείας καταψευδόμενον παρωσάμενοι τὸ μονότροπον καὶ μονοπρόσωπον τῆς ἀληθείας ἀσπασώμεθα. ἁβροδίαιτον ὀνειδίζων νεανίαν ὁ Σοφοκλῆς λέγει· γυναικομίμοις ἐμπρέπεις ἐσθήμασιν. ὡς γὰρ στρατιώτου καὶ ναύτου καὶ ἄρχοντος, οὕτως δὲ καὶ σώφρονός ἐστιν οἰκεία στολὴ ἡ ἀπερίεργος καὶ εὐσχήμων καὶ καθάριος. παρ᾿ ὃ καὶ ὁ ἐν τῷ νόμῳ περὶ τῆς λέπρας διὰ Μωυσέως τεθεὶς νόμος τὸ ποικίλον καὶ πολύστικτον ὡς οὐχ ὅσιον ἀπωθεῖται ταῖς ποικίλαις τοῦ ὄφεως φολίσιν ἐοικός. τὸν γοῦν μηκέτι διηνθισμένον ποικιλίᾳ χρωμάτων, ὅλον δὲ λευκωθέντα δι᾿ ὅλων ἀπὸ κεφαλῆς ἄκρας ἄχρι ποδῶν ἐσχάτων καθαρὸν εἶναι ἐθέλει, ἵνα κατὰ τὴν ἀπὸ τοῦ σώματος μετάβασιν τὸ ποικίλον καὶ πανοῦργον τῆς διανοίας μεθέμενοι πάθος τὸ ἀποίκιλτον καὶ ἀνενδοίαστον τῆς ἀληθείας ἁπλοῦν ἀγαπήσωμεν χρῶμα. ὁ δὲ καὶ ἐν τούτῳ ἄρα ζηλωτὴν Μωυσέως, ὁ πάντα ἄριστος Πλάτων, ὑφὴν ἐκείνην ἀποδέχεται, ᾗ μὴ πλέον ἔργον πρόσεστι γυναικὸς σώφρονος· »χρώματα δὲ λευκὰ πρέποντα ἂν εἴη σεμνότητι καὶ ἄλλοθι« λέγει »καὶ ἐν ὑφῇ· βάμματα δὲ μὴ προσφέρειν ἀλλ᾿ ἢ πρὸς τὰ πολέμου κοσμήματα.« εἰρηνικοῖς ἄρα ἀνθρώποις καὶ φωτεινοῖς κατάλληλον τὸ λευκόν. ὡς οὖν τὰ σημεῖα τὰ ἐγγυτάτω ὄντα τῶν αἰτίων παρόντα σημαίνει, μᾶλλον δὲ δείκνυσι τὴν τοῦ ἀποτελέσαντος ὕπαρξιν, οἷον καπνὸς μὲν πῦρ, εὔχροια δὲ καὶ εὐσφυξία ὑγίειαν, οὕτως καὶ παρ᾿ ἡμῖν ἡ τοιάδε στολὴ τοῦ ἤθους τὴν κατάστασιν ἐνδείκνυται. καθάριος δὲ καὶ ἀφελὴς ἡ σωφροσύνη, ἐπεὶ ἡ μὲν καθαριότης ἕξις ἐστὶν παρασκευαστικὴ διαίτης καθαρᾶς καὶ ἀμιγοῦς αἰσχροῖς, ἡ δὲ ἀφέλεια ἕξις ἀφαιρετικὴ τῶν περιττῶν. ἡ δὲ στερεὰ ἐσθὴς καὶ μάλιστα ἡ ἄγναφος ἀποστέγει τὸ θερμὸν τὸ ἐν τῷ σώματι, οὐχ ὅτι ἐν αὑτῇ ἔχει τὴν θερμότητα ἡ ἐσθής, ἀλλ᾿ ὅτι τὴν ἐν τῷ σώματι ἐξιοῦσαν ἀναστρέφει καὶ πάροδον αὐτῇ οὐ παρέχει, εἰ δὲ καὶ ἐμπέσοι τις, συλλαβοῦσα αὐτὴν ἐν αὑτῇ ἔχει καὶ ὑπ᾿ αὐτῆς θερμανθεῖσα ἀντιθερμαίνει τὸ σῶμα, δι᾿ ὃ καὶ χειμῶνος μάλιστα ταύτῃ χρηστέον· εὔκολος δὲ αὕτη· εὐκολία δέ ἐστιν ἕξις ἀπέριττος προσδεκτικὴ τῶν πρὸς τὸ ἀνελλιπὲς ἐξαρκούντων εἰς τὸν κατὰ λόγον, τὸν ὑγιῆ καὶ μακάριον, βίον. κεχρήσθω δὲ καὶ ἡ γυνὴ τῇ λιτῇ στολῇ καὶ τῇ σεμνῇ, μαλακωτέρᾳ δὲ μᾶλλον ἢ προσῆκεν ἀνδρί, πλὴν οὐ τέλεον ἀπηρυθριακυίᾳ, οὐ διαρρεούσῃ τῇ μαλακότητι.
pass_a_gloss: For this reason, therefore, we must not completely cut off wearing gold and using softer clothing, but we must restrain the irrational impulses, lest they lead us into luxury, carrying us away under much negligence; for luxury is terrible, having slipped into excess, and it makes one leap and dance and throw off the charioteer and the tutor, who, looking from afar, guides and carries the human horse, the irrational part of the soul, towards salvation, concerning pleasures and desires, and it makes one fond of ornaments and gold and varied clothing and other vanity; having this in mind, the thing that was said in a holy manner, 'having your conduct among the nations good, so that in what they speak against you as evil-doers, they may, seeing your good works, glorify God'; the tutor, therefore, gives us permission to use simple clothing and white color, as we said before, so that, not being fond of varied art, but of natural things, we may reject everything that is deceptive and false and welcome the simple and single-faced truth; Sophocles, reproaching a young man for luxury, says, 'you are conspicuous in womanly clothing'; for just as a soldier and a sailor and a ruler have their own proper dress, simple and modest and clean, so also does a self-controlled person; and the law in the law concerning leprosy, given through Moses, rejects the varied and much-spun as not holy, being like the varied scales of a snake; for it wants the one who is no longer dyed with varied colors, but completely whitened from head to foot, to be clean, so that, having changed from the body, we may love the simple and unchanging color of truth, having put away the varied and cunning passion of the mind; and Plato, the best of all, who is an imitator of Moses in this, accepts this kind of weaving, in which no more work is added than is fitting for a self-controlled woman; 'white colors, therefore, are suitable for dignity and also for weaving', he says, 'and do not apply dyes except for war ornaments'; therefore, white is suitable for peaceful and bright people; just as the signs that are closest to the causes, being present, signify, or rather show, the existence of the one who brought them to completion, such as smoke signifies fire, and good color and good breathing signify health, so also among us this kind of dress signifies the condition of character; for self-control is pure and simple, since purity is a habit that prepares for a pure and unmixed diet, and simplicity is a habit that removes what is superfluous; and a thick and especially a unwashed garment keeps the body warm, not because the garment has warmth in itself, but because it turns back the warmth that is escaping from the body and does not provide a passage for it, and if some cold air should come in, it holds it in itself and, having been warmed by it, warms the body in return, for which reason we must use it especially in winter; and it is also easy to use; ease of use is a habit that is without superfluity, receptive of what is sufficient for a rational, healthy, and happy life; let the woman also use simple and dignified dress, softer than what is fitting for a man, but not completely given over to softness, not overflowing with softness.

choices.why: The word is used to describe excessive and indulgent behavior.
The word is used to describe a person who guides and teaches, like a charioteer guides a horse.

bible_refs.note: having your conduct among the nations good

pass_b_english: For this reason, then, we must not entirely forbid wearing gold or using softer clothing, but we must restrain the irrational impulses, lest they lead us into luxury, carrying us away under the weight of excessive negligence. Luxury is terrible; once it has slipped into excess, it makes one leap and dance and throw off both the charioteer and the tutor, who, looking from afar and pulling back the reins, guides and carries the human horse — the irrational part of the soul concerned with pleasures and shameful desires, ornaments, gold, varied clothing, and every other vanity — toward salvation. Keeping this in mind, we recall the holy saying: "Keep your conduct among the Gentiles good, so that when they speak against you as evildoers, they may see your good deeds and glorify God" (1 Peter 2:12). The tutor, therefore, gives us permission to use simple clothing and white color, as we said before, so that we may not cling to what is artificially variegated but to what is natural by birth, rejecting everything deceptive and false to the truth, and welcoming the single-minded and single-faced truth. Sophocles, reproaching a young man for luxury, says: "You are conspicuous in womanly garments." For just as a soldier, a sailor, and a ruler each have their own proper dress — simple, modest, and clean — so also does a self-controlled person. And the law concerning leprosy, given through Moses in the Law, rejects the variegated and heavily spun as unholy, since it resembles the variegated scales of a serpent. It demands that the one who is no longer dyed with varied colors, but completely whitened from head to foot, be clean, so that, having transitioned from the body, we may put away the variegated and cunning passion of the mind and love the simple, unchanging color of truth. Plato, the best of all, who in this matter is an imitator of Moses, accepts that kind of weaving in which no more work is added than befits a self-controlled woman. "White colors, therefore, are suitable for dignity and also for weaving," he says, "and dyes should not be applied except for war ornaments." White is therefore suitable for peaceful and bright people. Just as signs closest to their causes, by being present, signify — or rather show — the existence of the one who produced them, such as smoke indicates fire, and good color and good breathing indicate health, so among us this kind of dress indicates the condition of character. Self-control is pure and simple; purity is a habit that prepares for a pure and unmixed life, unmingled with shameful things, and simplicity is a habit that removes what is superfluous. A thick garment, especially an unwashed one, retains the body's warmth — not because the garment possesses warmth in itself, but because it turns back the warmth escaping from the body and gives it no passage out; and if some cold should enter, the garment holds it, warms it, and in turn warms the body. For this reason we must use such clothing especially in winter. It is also easy to use, and ease of use is a habit without superfluity, receptive of what suffices for a rational, healthy, and blessed life. Let the woman also use simple and dignified dress, softer than what befits a man, but not entirely given over to softness, not overflowing with it.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the complex metaphors of the charioteer/tutor and the horse. The scripture citation (1 Peter 2:12) is correctly identified and added as required. The distinction between 'purity' (καθαριότης) as a habit for diet and 'simplicity' (ἀφέλεια) as a habit for removing the superfluous is preserved. The technical description of the garment's thermal properties is rendered faithfully.
